idiom_name: stateless mixin class (plain base) + __slots__ at every level
implementation_notes: In CPython the instance layout, not the base count, decides size: a class that declares no attributes contributes no per-instance storage, so a mixin whose body is only methods costs nothing and the classic empty-base problem is already solved by the object model. Where instances are numerous the real cost is the per-instance __dict__ (and __weakref__), which __slots__ removes; the mixin must declare __slots__ = () and every subclass must redeclare __slots__ with only its new names, otherwise an ancestor without slots quietly reintroduces __dict__ and the saving disappears. The classic base-class form remains justified when the base must be part of the MRO for isinstance, ABC registration or cooperative super() calls - but the reason is typing and dispatch, never storage.
pitfalls: A subclass that omits __slots__ gets __dict__ back, silently negating the memory win for that level and all of its own subclasses.
If any ancestor in the MRO lacks __slots__, slotted subclasses still carry __dict__, so the hierarchy must be slotted from the top down.
__slots__ also removes __weakref__ support, and multiple inheritance from two slotted parents whose instance layouts conflict raises TypeError at class creation.
